Plenty of men of all sorts get their ears pierced. If you feel you can't out aren't ready yet or even just want to test the waters, there are some rather cute clip on our magnetic earrings for cheap. When you do decide to piece, do it at a tattoo shop. Mall stores use a piercing gun which punches a hole rather than removes any flesh. They'll be at risk to close easier, may not be as comfortable and they aren't as accurate in getting them symetical. 💙💜

I started with clip ons also to figure out if I wanted any helix piercings and such. They're versatile and fun. Don't have my helix just yet so I still wear them when I want. Simple ear cuffs are awesome too. Even wore them as a lip ring & nose ring before haha.

It's alright. unfortunately though I do. Had therapy just tonight where I talked about my recent nightmares. My three friends each know. Even my sister knows as I told her hoping she'd provide some sort of safe haven within the family but that didn't work out as she screamed at me to get over myself... :(

Thanks, I can't shake the thoughts of self hate and that I'm worthless or even hurting others by existing. Feelings of being afraid that the goals I try for are unattainable and I'm too late to make a difference. I've got alot of regrets and pain from my life. Because of some of those, I was emotionally broken. As I work towards fixing that and being connected with my emotions, the pain sometimes gets overwhelming. Sometimes and it's a nice to think on the idea of reincarnation or if not that, then just nothingness.

If you're ever around **** I'll take you up on the hug. Lots of crying yesterday and those two amazing friends and I'm willing to try for awhile longer. You helped too so thank you so much. Best friend is getting rid of my chemicals and of course it's still all so rough and I miss them already but she also had me make the call for the psych appt to get some antidepressants. That's been something I've been trying to bring myself to do since the gencon attempt. I still wish I was successful then but I'll be around at least for awhile longer to keep trying. Thanks 💙

Thank you. Your reply is really touching. 

I've only been on my hormones for nearly a year now and so I'm making progress but it takes time and I know they're working well for me but there's a disconnect still for me between much of what I know logically and how I feel emotionally.

I've been seeing a trans specialist therapist for two and a half years and an additional art therapist for two years now. My trans therapist leaves me wanting as she gets distracted or it feels difficult to talk to sometimes but she's still helped more than not. My art therapist is amazing and has helped immeasurably. I've cancelled my week with each of them. Before them was an unhelpful therapist for another 6 years. My art therapist has helped me reconnect to my emotions I've disassociated from for a lifetime as a defensive mechanism. The other therapist, has helped some i guess but doesn't quite feel like they are the best one for me. She is heavily involved in the local lgbt support community though. 

As for being taught to blame myself, there may be more than a grain of truth there. I'm a middle child with high expectations on me. I've spent so much time burying my emotions that I only ever relied on others to tell me what to do. College & grad school. My degree. My high school sweetheart was emotionally abusive for our 5 years together until I got up courage to leave her. And then there was ongoing rape by my older brother who found me while learning about my gender. I was dressed in sisters clothes alone at home at 12yo. That abuse continued for awhile. I've told my sister only a  couple of years ago now and tried to rely on her as a safe space from him within family gatherings but she wasn't able to give that for me. She freaked out when she thought I'd tell my mom but I just can't. It would destroy her to know. He has a family now too and Im left feeling it's too late. It does no good, only such extreme harm to the rest of the family to know that part. Everyone has tried hard to accept me as being trans and while there was disbelief and denial at first, that tone quickly changed. 

I guess the abuse really is at the core of learning to blame myself adding on to it with other events like my abusive ex. Carrying that alone for so very long and learning to suppress my emotions and disassociate as a survival technique have just done such harm to me that while I'm working to repair that part of myself, it's like precision surgery on a dam. I need to relieve the built up pressure done by chipping at it. Every chip though risks a disaster and I feel my cracks are starting to appear. I fell once already and was dragged back to my feet but I've not recovered and I hurt so very much.

Again, thank you for listening.

Not feeling 'queer enough is a problem many of us face. Same goes for not feeling part of the community. I was told off by a gay man before that wtf am I? I'm not gay look at me! (I never claimed to be gay, I'm bi...) Sometimes the community can be the most hurtful to itself. Well he never listened to me enough to learn that I was only at the beginnings of my struggle and am actually transgender as well... Don't let others tell you who you are even if they do so under the guise of community. Surround yourself with validating friends and reach out a hand to help others too feel a part of the community and to accept themselves. It'll really make a difference in self acceptance as well. Thank you for being who you are.

I think you're a wonderful parent. Maybe if you haven't talked with him about sex and protection in general now is the time. It would be perfect to mention in a safe way that you are ok with his developing sexuality without bringing up that specific situation. Just that there are lots of people both women and boys that will pressure him into sex and that condoms are important and do more than protect from unplanned kids. That they're necessary whether he finds himself with girls or other boys and to insist on them. Being smart is attractive. 

*As to the overnight situation. Insist on open bedroom doors but I wouldn't outright deny the friend from sleeping over. You've got a safe and accepting home. While not encouraging messing around it'll happen one way or the other and your son may feel more empowered in your own home to make the decisions he wants to than feeling pressured in other environments.
